In summary, our research is concerned with
the accessibility of sulfite pulp fibers to proteins and the influence of enzymatic attack on the accessibility.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a large proportion of fibers is not fully accessible to enzymic attack.
the penetration of lignin peroxidases into the fibers is not restricted, but the interaction between enzyme and substrate is.
the accessibility of the fibers to enzymatic attack depends on a complex interplay between morphological, chemical, and structural factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the accessibility of the fibers to enzymatic attack is a very important factor in the enzymatic bleaching of pulp.
the penetration of lignin peroxidases is not a limiting factor in enzymatic bleaching.
the accessibility of lignin peroxidases to residual lignin and other proteins to the fibers is not uniform in the fibers of the pulp.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enzymatic bleaching efficiency is not limited by the accessibility of lignin peroxidases to lignin in the pulp fibers.
the accessibility of lignin peroxidases and other enzymes to residual lignin in the pulp fibers is highly dependent on fiber morphology and the degree of lignin degradation.

enzymatic bleaching with lignin peroxi-dases is a promising alternative to the use of chlorine-based bleaching chemicals, provided that the enzymes can reach their target substrates in the pulp fibers.
